title: Remote MCP connector profiles for ChatGPT, Claude, and generic clients

phases.objective: Prove one disabled-by-default remote MCP surface can classify and serve ChatGPT, Claude, and generic approved clients without changing platform authorization or exposing client-specific business logic.

e2e_journeys.actor: ChatGPT, Claude, or another approved standards-compliant remote MCP client
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: POST /mcp initialize and tools/list using an allowed Origin or a non-browser client without Origin
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Every client receives the same bounded read-only protocol and tool contract, while unapproved browser origins fail closed and client classification grants no platform authority.
steps: Resolve neutral REMOTE_MCP configuration with temporary CHATGPT_MCP compatibility aliases.
Classify known ChatGPT and Claude origins only for operational metadata.
Initialize the shared Streamable HTTP endpoint using each supported client profile.
List the same read-only tools and verify annotations remain unchanged.
Reject a browser Origin outside the explicit allowlist.
assertions: ChatGPT and Claude use the same canonical /mcp resource and tool catalog.
A generic client can use the standards contract without a platform-specific handler.
Missing Origin does not bypass OAuth or server-side authorization for protected tools.
Client-profile detection never selects tenant, workspace, Brand, resource, connection, capability, or operation authority.
The existing CHATGPT_MCP environment contract remains a temporary backward-compatible alias.

phases.objective: Provide a disabled-by-default OAuth 2.1 authorization server profile with allowlisted dynamic registration, a short-lived server-signed consent request, PKCE S256, a dedicated signing key, exact resource and token-to-grant identity binding, refresh rotation, durable revocation, and read-scope enforcement for the shared MCP resource.

e2e_journeys.actor: Claude, ChatGPT, or a generic registered remote MCP OAuth client plus an active platform user
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Allowlisted dynamic registration followed by /auth/mcp/oauth/authorize, signed consent /code, /token, protected tools/call, refresh, and /revoke
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: An allowlisted registered client receives a resource-bound scoped token only after a signed authorization request and explicit consent, can call only authorized read tools, rotates refresh tokens once, and loses access after revocation or any client, user, tenant, subject, scope, resource, or grant mismatch.
steps: Reject DCR redirects whose exact non-loopback Origin is not present in the server-controlled allowlist.
Register an exact HTTPS redirect and bounded read scopes for a public or confidential client.
Validate client, redirect, state, resource, scopes, and PKCE before issuing a five-minute server-signed authorization request.
Require an active platform user plus explicit consent and reject missing, expired, or tampered signed requests.
Issue an opaque short-lived authorization code bound to client, redirect, resource, scopes, user, tenant, and S256 challenge.
Verify the PKCE verifier before atomically consuming the authorization code.
Issue a short-lived JWT with the dedicated OAuth signing key and an opaque refresh token backed by an active durable grant.
Validate issuer, audience, resource, purpose, azp, client, subject, user, tenant, scope, JTI, expiry, and exact active-grant parity before protected tool dispatch.
Rotate the refresh token and mark the previous grant unusable.
Revoke the access or refresh token and fail subsequent protected calls closed.
assertions: OAuth and DCR routes return 404 while their feature flags are disabled.
DCR fails closed without an approved redirect-Origin allowlist and rejects lookalike or unapproved Origins.
Unknown or mismatched redirects, resources, clients, scopes, and PKCE values are rejected.
Missing consent and missing, tampered, or expired signed authorization requests cannot issue an authorization code.
The Remote MCP OAuth signing key is distinct from the platform user JWT key.
A failed PKCE attempt does not consume a valid authorization code.
Authorization codes are single-use after successful verification.
Access tokens are valid only for the exact remote MCP resource and exact active grant, including matching azp, client, user, tenant, subject, scopes, and JTI.
Refresh rotation allows at most one successor grant and prevents replay of the previous refresh token.
Revocation is checked during every protected tools/call request.
No client secret, signed authorization request, access token, refresh token, authorization code, or raw grant is emitted in logs or MCP tool results.

phases.objective: Prove dependency faults, concurrent refresh races, grant-store outages, signed-request expiry and replay handling, metadata drift, abuse controls, signing-key rotation, and recovery independently for each supported client profile.

Apply the migration, provision the dedicated signing key and redirect-Origin allowlist, and connect the exact candidate from MCP Inspector, ChatGPT Developer mode, Claude Custom Connector settings, and a neutral programmatic client against an authorized non-production endpoint.

Verify production DNS, TLS, routing, exact SHA, OAuth linkage, client registrations, tenant isolation, monitoring, disable controls, signing-key rotation, backup, and rollback for every advertised client profile.
